An aircraft's clearance (in its panel) is a filled chip in its color; a write-up's status is a muted chip; Overdue and Needs scheduling are orange outlined chips; severity is bare text. Clearance started as bare red text and read the same as a High severity label beneath it. All chips share one box: trimmed to the capital height with equal insets, so they line up on the text baseline next to them.
   116	
   117	## Architecture
   118	
   119	### A1. Language and framework?
   120	**Decision:** Python with FastAPI.
   121	**Why:** Small and explicit. Pydantic validates input at the boundary, and pytest with TestClient makes route tests easy. Django brings more ceremony than this needs; TypeScript only pays off with a separate JS frontend.
   122	
   123	### A2. Server-rendered pages or a separate JS app?
   124	**Decision:** Server-rendered HTML templates with plain forms, redirecting after each POST.
   125	**Why:** One process, one language, nothing to build. Decision 12 only needs status to be correct on page load, so a single-page app's extra toolchain buys nothing.
   126	
   127	### A3. Database and how we talk to it?
   128	**Decision:** SQLite through SQLAlchemy. Tables are created on startup; no migration tool.
   129	**Why:** No setup for the reviewer, and SQLite easily handles 1,500 aircraft. A transaction makes each change and its audit entry commit together. A schema change means deleting the DB file and reseeding, which is fine for a demo.
   130	
   131	### A4. What shape are the routes?
   132	**Decision:** One POST route per action (schedule or reschedule, unschedule, start, resolve, cancel, change severity, edit description), each with its own required fields and its own audit entry. No JSON API.
   133	**Why:** Each action has different rules and inputs, so separate routes keep validation explicit. A generic edit route would have to infer what happened. Nothing in the brief needs JSON.
   134	
   135	### A5. How does someone run it?
   136	**Decision:** One `uv run` command. It seeds demo data when the DB file doesn't exist; a reset command wipes and reseeds.
   137	**Why:** uv fetches the right Python and dependencies itself, which avoids the most common way take-homes fail to start. No external services.
   138	
   139	### A6. How is testing set up?
   140	**Decision:** pytest in two layers. Unit tests on plain Python rule functions (transitions, grounding, overdue, date checks), written first. Route tests through TestClient on a fresh SQLite database per test. No browser tests; the UI is checked by hand.
   141	**Why:** Rules get fast, pinpointed tests for TDD; route tests cover what only exists with a database (audit entries, validation errors, the fleet page). Browser tests are a time sink at this scope.
   142	
   143	### A7. Where is "cleared to fly" computed?
   144	**Decision:** In one Python rule function. The fleet page loads all open write-ups in one query, groups them by aircraft, and applies it.
   145	**Why:** One source of truth that the unit tests cover. At 1,500 aircraft that's milliseconds. At far larger scale it would move into SQL.
   146	
   147	### A8. What counts as "today" for Overdue and past-date checks?
   148	**Decision:** The server's local date. Scheduled dates are calendar dates with no time. Today is passed into the rule functions so tests can fix it. Audit timestamps are stored in UTC.
   149	**Why:** Simple and predictable. An airline spanning time zones could disagree about "today" near midnight; per-base time zones would fix that but aren't worth it here.
   150	
   151	### A9. Where do "who" and "why" live, and who has to give a name?
   152	**Decision:** The write-up row holds its current state plus who filed it and when. Every later change is an audit-log row with who, when, the old and new value, and a note. A name is required on every action, not only filing and resolving. Who fixed it and what was done live only on the resolve entry; cancel notes and severity reasons likewise.
   153	**Why:** Decision 7 promises a history of who changed what, which needs a name on every change. This extends decision 5. Keeping each fact in one place avoids resolution columns on the write-up that duplicate the log.
   154	**Note:** The row holds only the current severity, so the History line "Filed as …" takes the severity at filing from the log: what the first severity change replaced, or the current one if it never changed. It first printed the current severity, which was wrong after a downgrade. Storing a second severity column or logging a filing entry would duplicate what the log already says.
   155	
   156	### A10. How much is enforced by the database itself?
   157	**Decision:** Foreign keys are enforced (SQLite leaves them off unless every connection turns them on). CHECK constraints cover: allowed severity, status and audit-entry values; non-empty names and descriptions; the scheduled date matching the status (empty when Unscheduled; set when Scheduled, In progress or Resolved; either when Canceled, since a write-up can be canceled before it was ever scheduled); and a note on every resolve, cancel and severity change.
   158	**Why:** A second line of defense against bad seed data, manual edits and future bugs. This is a deliberate exception to CLAUDE.md's "don't guard against impossible states". Two rules stay in code only: which transitions are allowed (a CHECK sees one row, not the previous state) and no dates in the past (SQLite rejects `date('now')` in a CHECK constraint).
   159	
   160	### A11. How is the seed data built?
   161	**Decision:** Through the same actions the app uses, run with backdated clocks, rather than inserted rows. 30 aircraft; the first twelve each demonstrate one situation (grounded in each open state, grounded by two Highs, cleared after a fix, after a downgrade, after a no-fault cancel, cleared despite an overdue Medium, and so on). A test fails if the seed stops covering every status, severity, audit entry type, overdue case and aircraft situation.
   162	**Why:** Seeded write-ups and audit entries are guaranteed to be ones the app could produce, and the demo can't silently lose a case.
   163	
   164	### A12. Indexes?
   165	**Decision:** Write-ups are indexed on (aircraft, status) for an aircraft's page and on status for the fleet page's "all open write-ups" query. Audit entries are indexed on write-up.
   166	**Why:** The fleet page filters by status alone, which the (aircraft, status) index from the reviewed model can't serve.
   167	
   168	### A13. How much frontend tooling?
   169	**Decision:** One hand-written CSS file. Disclosure uses native HTML (`<details>`, separate pages). One small script keeps the board's scroll position across page loads; nothing depends on it.
   170	**Why:** Follows from A2. Every action is a plain form POST, so a script would add a second way for things to break. The exception: every click loads a new page, and without a script the board jumped back to the top each time, which made a long fleet list unusable. The script only restores the scroll position; with it off, every action still works.
   171	**Note:** Started as zero JavaScript; changed after trying the board.

Reproduced two of the candidates; reporting findings now.

findings.summary: A rejected action whose form no longer exists on the re-rendered card returns a 400 page with no error message anywhere.
findings.short_summary: Stale-action errors render nowhere
findings.failure_scenario: User A starts (or cancels/resolves) write-up 1; user B, on a stale page, clicks Start work. RuleViolation sets form_id '1-start', but the card now shows only the Resolve form (or no card at all if the write-up closed), so error_for never matches: B gets a 400 board with no explanation. Reproduced: second POST /writeups/1/start returns 400 without the message in the body.

findings.summary: Actions read the write-up, check the rule in Python, then write, with no row version or status guard, so two concurrent requests can both pass the check on the same stale state.
findings.short_summary: Read-check-write race on write-up status
findings.failure_scenario: Sync endpoints run in the threadpool. A posts cancel and B posts resolve on the same in-progress write-up at once: both load status=in_progress, both pass rules, both commit. The row ends in whichever wrote last and the audit log holds both 'canceled' and 'resolved' events, a transition the rules forbid. A version_id_col on Writeup would turn the second into a StaleDataError.

findings.summary: strftime('%-d') is a glibc/BSD extension and raises ValueError on Windows, in both the day and local_time filters.
findings.short_summary: '%-d' strftime crashes on Windows
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer runs the take-home on Windows and opens any aircraft panel: the History timeline and card dates call day/local_time, strftime raises 'Invalid format string', and the page is a 500. The board alone loads, every aircraft link fails.

findings.summary: invalid_form indexes FIELD_LABELS with the failing field name, which only has entries for severity and scheduled_date; any other field failing validation raises KeyError inside the exception handler.
findings.short_summary: KeyError in validation handler gives a 500
findings.failure_scenario: A multipart POST that sends actor (or note/description/reported_by) as a file part fails string validation; FIELD_LABELS['actor'] raises KeyError and the request ends as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Reproduced with POST /writeups/1/start files={'actor': ...}. Needs a hand-built request, not reachable from the app's own forms.

findings.summary: local_time converts stored UTC timestamps using now.tzinfo, a fixed offset for the current moment, so times from the other side of a DST change are shown an hour off.
findings.short_summary: History times off by an hour across DST
findings.failure_scenario: Server in US Eastern, today in November (UTC-5). A write-up filed at 14:00 local on 30 October (UTC-4, stored as 18:00 UTC) is shown in History and on its card as 13:00. at.replace(tzinfo=UTC).astimezone() would use the zone's offset for that date; the tests' fixed-offset clock hides this.

findings.summary: Seeding is keyed on the DB file not existing, but create_db creates the file before seed runs, so an interrupted or failed first seed leaves a permanently empty fleet.
findings.short_summary: Failed first seed leaves an empty DB forever
findings.failure_scenario: First run is interrupted (Ctrl-C, or seed raises) after create_all but before seed's single commit. maintenance.db now exists with empty tables, so every later run skips seeding and shows '0 aircraft' with no way to add any in the UI, until someone knows to pass --reset. Checking for zero aircraft instead of file existence avoids it.

findings.summary: The saved scroll offset uses one sessionStorage key for every board URL, so it is restored onto pages showing a different list.
findings.short_summary: Scroll offset restored onto a different list
findings.failure_scenario: Scroll down to N425, then search 'N4' or follow 'Clear search': the new result list loads scrolled to the old pixel offset rather than its top, so the first matches (the grounded group) are off screen. The offset only makes sense when the list is the same, i.e. same q and hide values.

findings.summary: The search form carries the hidden groups but not the open aircraft, so searching closes the aircraft panel, unlike every other link and form on the board.
findings.short_summary: Searching closes the open aircraft panel
findings.failure_scenario: On desktop with N403's panel open, typing a tail fragment and pressing Search submits only q and hide; the aircraft parameter is dropped and the panel disappears, losing any half-typed form in it. board_linker treats tail as state to keep; the search form does not.

findings.summary: timeline lazy-loads events once per write-up and renders the aircraft's entire history on every panel load.
findings.short_summary: N+1 event queries and unbounded timeline
findings.failure_scenario: Every panel view and every failed-form re-render issues one SELECT per write-up the aircraft has ever had, then renders all of them. Fine for the seed; an aircraft with a few hundred historical write-ups costs hundreds of queries per click, which sits badly with decision 9 (shouldn't fall over at 10-50x). selectinload(Writeup.events) on the aircraft query makes it two queries.

findings.summary: Docstrings on board_linker and render_failure restate what the function does, against the project CLAUDE.md comment rule.
findings.short_summary: Docstrings describe what, not why
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE.md (repo root): "Almost no comments. A comment explains *why*, never *what*." main.py:88 "Builds links from the current board, changing only what the caller names." and main.py:134 "Re-renders the aircraft the failed form belonged to, with the message and what was typed." both describe what the code does.

findings.summary: A rejected action whose form no longer exists on the re-rendered card returns a 400 page with no error message anywhere.
findings.short_summary: Stale-action errors render nowhere

findings.summary: Actions read the write-up, check the rule in Python, then write, with no row version or status guard, so two concurrent requests can both pass the check on the same stale state.
findings.short_summary: Read-check-write race on write-up status
findings.failure_scenario: Sync endpoints run in the threadpool. A posts cancel and B posts resolve on the same in-progress write-up at once: both load status=in_progress, both pass rules, both commit. The row ends in whichever wrote last and the audit log holds both 'canceled' and 'resolved' events, a transition the rules forbid. A version_id_col on Writeup would turn the second into a StaleDataError.

findings.summary: strftime('%-d') is a glibc/BSD extension and raises ValueError on Windows, in both the day and local_time filters.

findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer runs the take-home on Windows and opens any aircraft panel: the History timeline and card dates call day/local_time, strftime raises 'Invalid format string', and the page is a 500. The board alone loads, every aircraft link fails.

findings.summary: invalid_form indexes FIELD_LABELS with the failing field name, which only has entries for severity and scheduled_date; any other field failing validation raises KeyError inside the exception handler.

findings.summary: local_time converts stored UTC timestamps using now.tzinfo, a fixed offset for the current moment, so times from the other side of a DST change are shown an hour off.
findings.short_summary: History times off by an hour across DST
findings.failure_scenario: Server in US Eastern, today in November (UTC-5). findings.summary: Seeding is keyed on the DB file not existing, but create_db creates the file before seed runs, so an interrupted or failed first seed leaves a permanently empty fleet.
findings.short_summary: Failed first seed leaves an empty DB forever
findings.failure_scenario: First run is interrupted (Ctrl-C, or seed raises) after create_all but before seed's single commit. maintenance.db now exists with empty tables, so every later run skips seeding and shows '0 aircraft' with no way to add any in the UI, until someone knows to pass --reset. findings.summary: timeline lazy-loads events once per write-up and renders the aircraft's entire history on every panel load.

def test_action_the_writeup_has_moved_past_still_shows_why(client):
    file(client)

    assert "Write-up #1 has changed since this page loaded." in response.text
    assert "A canceled write-up" in response.text
EOF

### A14. What does someone see when they act on a write-up that changed under them?
**Decision:** The action is rejected and the reason shows at the top of the aircraft panel, prefixed with which write-up changed. Other rejections (a blank name, a past date) still show inside the form that was submitted.
**Why:** The card only offers the actions its status allows, so a status rejection means the page was out of date (someone else acted, or a double submit), and by then the submitted form is no longer on the card. The message used to be attached to that missing form, so the page came back as a 400 with no explanation. Status rejections are their own exception type so the route can tell the two cases apart without knowing which forms each status shows.
EOF

findings.summary: A rejected action whose form no longer exists on the re-rendered card returns a 400 page with no error message anywhere.
findings.short_summary: Stale-action errors render nowhere
findings.failure_scenario: User A starts (or cancels/resolves) write-up 1; user B, on a stale page, clicks Start work. RuleViolation sets form_id '1-start', but the card now shows only the Resolve form (or no card at all if the write-up closed), so error_for never matches: B gets a 400 board with no explanation. Reproduced: second POST /writeups/1/start returns 400 without the message in the body.

findings.summary: Actions read the write-up, check the rule in Python, then write, with no row version or status guard, so two concurrent requests can both pass the check on the same stale state.
findings.short_summary: Read-check-write race on write-up status
findings.failure_scenario: Sync endpoints run in the threadpool. A posts cancel and B posts resolve on the same in-progress write-up at once: both load status=in_progress, both pass rules, both commit. The row ends in whichever wrote last and the audit log holds both 'canceled' and 'resolved' events, a transition the rules forbid. A version_id_col on Writeup would turn the second into a StaleDataError.

findings.summary: strftime('%-d') is a glibc/BSD extension and raises ValueError on Windows, in both the day and local_time filters.
findings.short_summary: '%-d' strftime crashes on Windows
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer runs the take-home on Windows and opens any aircraft panel: the History timeline and card dates call day/local_time, strftime raises 'Invalid format string', and the page is a 500. The board alone loads, every aircraft link fails.

findings.summary: invalid_form indexes FIELD_LABELS with the failing field name, which only has entries for severity and scheduled_date; any other field failing validation raises KeyError inside the exception handler.
findings.short_summary: KeyError in validation handler gives a 500
findings.failure_scenario: A multipart POST that sends actor (or note/description/reported_by) as a file part fails string validation; FIELD_LABELS['actor'] raises KeyError and the request ends as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Reproduced with POST /writeups/1/start files={'actor': ...}. Needs a hand-built request, not reachable from the app's own forms.

findings.summary: local_time converts stored UTC timestamps using now.tzinfo, a fixed offset for the current moment, so times from the other side of a DST change are shown an hour off.
findings.short_summary: History times off by an hour across DST
findings.failure_scenario: Server in US Eastern, today in November (UTC-5). A write-up filed at 14:00 local on 30 October (UTC-4, stored as 18:00 UTC) is shown in History and on its card as 13:00. at.replace(tzinfo=UTC).astimezone() would use the zone's offset for that date; the tests' fixed-offset clock hides this.

findings.summary: Seeding is keyed on the DB file not existing, but create_db creates the file before seed runs, so an interrupted or failed first seed leaves a permanently empty fleet.
findings.short_summary: Failed first seed leaves an empty DB forever
findings.failure_scenario: First run is interrupted (Ctrl-C, or seed raises) after create_all but before seed's single commit. maintenance.db now exists with empty tables, so every later run skips seeding and shows '0 aircraft' with no way to add any in the UI, until someone knows to pass --reset. Checking for zero aircraft instead of file existence avoids it.

findings.summary: The saved scroll offset uses one sessionStorage key for every board URL, so it is restored onto pages showing a different list.
findings.short_summary: Scroll offset restored onto a different list
findings.failure_scenario: Scroll down to N425, then search 'N4' or follow 'Clear search': the new result list loads scrolled to the old pixel offset rather than its top, so the first matches (the grounded group) are off screen. The offset only makes sense when the list is the same, i.e. same q and hide values.

findings.summary: The search form carries the hidden groups but not the open aircraft, so searching closes the aircraft panel, unlike every other link and form on the board.
findings.short_summary: Searching closes the open aircraft panel
findings.failure_scenario: On desktop with N403's panel open, typing a tail fragment and pressing Search submits only q and hide; the aircraft parameter is dropped and the panel disappears, losing any half-typed form in it. board_linker treats tail as state to keep; the search form does not.

findings.summary: timeline lazy-loads events once per write-up and renders the aircraft's entire history on every panel load.
findings.short_summary: N+1 event queries and unbounded timeline
findings.failure_scenario: Every panel view and every failed-form re-render issues one SELECT per write-up the aircraft has ever had, then renders all of them.     assert load(session, writeup_id).status == Status.canceled

### A15. What if two people act on the same write-up at the same moment?
**Decision:** The first change wins and the second is rejected with the same "has changed since this page loaded" message as A14. Each write-up row carries a version number that every update checks and bumps.
**Why:** An action reads the write-up, checks the rule, then writes. Two requests in flight together could both pass the check on the same state, leaving a write-up both canceled and resolved in the audit log. The version check makes the database refuse the second write, which no check in Python can do. It is a new column, so an existing database needs `--reset` (A3).
EOF

message. Existing databases need --reset for the new column.

input.description: Confirm a clean tree, the final test count and the new commits

findings.summary: A rejected action whose form no longer exists on the re-rendered card returns a 400 page with no error message anywhere.
findings.short_summary: Stale-action errors render nowhere
findings.failure_scenario: User A starts (or cancels/resolves) write-up 1; user B, on a stale page, clicks Start work. RuleViolation sets form_id '1-start', but the card now shows only the Resolve form (or no card at all if the write-up closed), so error_for never matches: B gets a 400 board with no explanation. Reproduced: second POST /writeups/1/start returns 400 without the message in the body.

findings.summary: Actions read the write-up, check the rule in Python, then write, with no row version or status guard, so two concurrent requests can both pass the check on the same stale state.
findings.short_summary: Read-check-write race on write-up status
findings.failure_scenario: Sync endpoints run in the threadpool. A posts cancel and B posts resolve on the same in-progress write-up at once: both load status=in_progress, both pass rules, both commit. The row ends in whichever wrote last and the audit log holds both 'canceled' and 'resolved' events, a transition the rules forbid. A version_id_col on Writeup would turn the second into a StaleDataError.

findings.summary: strftime('%-d') is a glibc/BSD extension and raises ValueError on Windows, in both the day and local_time filters.
findings.short_summary: '%-d' strftime crashes on Windows
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer runs the take-home on Windows and opens any aircraft panel: the History timeline and card dates call day/local_time, strftime raises 'Invalid format string', and the page is a 500. The board alone loads, every aircraft link fails.

findings.summary: invalid_form indexes FIELD_LABELS with the failing field name, which only has entries for severity and scheduled_date; any other field failing validation raises KeyError inside the exception handler.
findings.short_summary: KeyError in validation handler gives a 500
findings.failure_scenario: A multipart POST that sends actor (or note/description/reported_by) as a file part fails string validation; FIELD_LABELS['actor'] raises KeyError and the request ends as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Reproduced with POST /writeups/1/start files={'actor': ...}. Needs a hand-built request, not reachable from the app's own forms.

findings.summary: local_time converts stored UTC timestamps using now.tzinfo, a fixed offset for the current moment, so times from the other side of a DST change are shown an hour off.
findings.short_summary: History times off by an hour across DST
findings.failure_scenario: Server in US Eastern, today in November (UTC-5). A write-up filed at 14:00 local on 30 October (UTC-4, stored as 18:00 UTC) is shown in History and on its card as 13:00. at.replace(tzinfo=UTC).astimezone() would use the zone's offset for that date; the tests' fixed-offset clock hides this.

findings.summary: Seeding is keyed on the DB file not existing, but create_db creates the file before seed runs, so an interrupted or failed first seed leaves a permanently empty fleet.
findings.short_summary: Failed first seed leaves an empty DB forever
findings.failure_scenario: First run is interrupted (Ctrl-C, or seed raises) after create_all but before seed's single commit. maintenance.db now exists with empty tables, so every later run skips seeding and shows '0 aircraft' with no way to add any in the UI, until someone knows to pass --reset. Checking for zero aircraft instead of file existence avoids it.

findings.summary: The saved scroll offset uses one sessionStorage key for every board URL, so it is restored onto pages showing a different list.
findings.short_summary: Scroll offset restored onto a different list
findings.failure_scenario: Scroll down to N425, then search 'N4' or follow 'Clear search': the new result list loads scrolled to the old pixel offset rather than its top, so the first matches (the grounded group) are off screen. The offset only makes sense when the list is the same, i.e. same q and hide values.

findings.summary: The search form carries the hidden groups but not the open aircraft, so searching closes the aircraft panel, unlike every other link and form on the board.
findings.short_summary: Searching closes the open aircraft panel
findings.failure_scenario: On desktop with N403's panel open, typing a tail fragment and pressing Search submits only q and hide; the aircraft parameter is dropped and the panel disappears, losing any half-typed form in it. board_linker treats tail as state to keep; the search form does not.

findings.summary: timeline lazy-loads events once per write-up and renders the aircraft's entire history on every panel load.
findings.short_summary: N+1 event queries and unbounded timeline
findings.failure_scenario: Every panel view and every failed-form re-render issues one SELECT per write-up the aircraft has ever had, then renders all of them. Fine for the seed; an aircraft with a few hundred historical write-ups costs hundreds of queries per click, which sits badly with decision 9 (shouldn't fall over at 10-50x). selectinload(Writeup.events) on the aircraft query makes it two queries.

```bash
uv run python -m app --reset
```

| Fix | Commit | How it was checked |
|---|---|---|
| Stale action shows its reason in the panel | `72f0e5b` | tests, and in the browser |
| Dates without `%-d`; times at the offset for their date | `8edcfdd` | tests; Windows itself not run |

| Version column rejects a concurrent write | `c870e0b` | test |

Browser checks ran against a throwaway server with its own database, not yours.

- **Search keeping the panel is a UX call.** "Clear search" used to close the panel explicitly, so the old behaviour may have been intended. Reverting is two lines in [board.html](app/templates/board.html).
- **The daylight-saving test is skipped on Windows**, because it sets the process time zone and Windows can't.
- **The scroll position survives hiding or showing a group**, since that link sits inside the list. Only a different search resets it.

content.text:
Fixed and committed as `deff87c`: the board now lays out its rows by its own width, so opening the panel on a mid-sized window gives the stacked layout instead of the crushed table.

The cause was that the stacked layout switched on the window width (640px), but the open panel takes 30rem off the board without the window changing. At your ~975px window the board had 495px and the description column had 29px. The fix is two lines in [app.css](app/static/app.css): the board is a query container, and the phone layout rule is now a container query at 40rem.

Checked in the browser on a throwaway server:

| Window | Panel | Board rows | Narrowest description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 375px | closed | stacked | 193px |
| 700px | closed | table | 250px |
| 961–1180px | open | stacked | 273–403px |
| 1280–1600px | open | table | 328–395px |

No horizontal scroll and no clipped flags at any of these.

You will need a hard refresh to see it, because the browser caches the stylesheet; my first reload still showed the old layout. The restart with `--reset` from before still applies too.

The 700px closed-panel case is the tightest table layout at 250px per description. If that reads cramped to you, raising the 40rem threshold is a one-number change.

content.text:
The current code is running at http://localhost:8793 and is open in the browser pane on N404TG. It uses a freshly seeded throwaway database, so anything you do there is disposable.

It is not on port 8000. Your old server (PID 34043, started 20:53) still holds that port with the old code and old-schema database. I tried to stop it and move `maintenance.db` aside, and the permission check blocked that as destructive, so I left both alone.

To run it on 8000 yourself, stop the old server in the terminal it is running in (Ctrl-C), then:

```bash
uv run python -m app --reset
```

`--reset` deletes `maintenance.db` and reseeds; the old one holds the seed data plus about one test action from this evening.

Should I stop the old server on port 8000 and reset its database, or is 8793 fine for testing?
